source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 70: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer:
Evaluation plan for a mixed short-prompt / long-generation LLM serving workload, focused on prefill/decode disaggregation.

1. Assumptions (state them, they bound every number below)
- Single model, fixed weights, fixed quantization and fixed engine version (e.g. vLLM X.Y). Any engine/version change invalidates the baseline.
- Hardware fixed: same GPU SKU, same NVLink/PCIe topology, MIG off, persistence mode on, clocks locked (nvidia-smi -lgc) to remove DVFS drift.
- Client is not the bottleneck: load generator runs on a separate host, has enough connections/cores, and its own latency floor is measured first with a null endpoint.
- Tokenizer-level accounting: TTFT/TPOT are defined on tokens, not bytes; streaming is enabled so first-token time is observable.

2. Metric definitions (unambiguous or the numbers are useless)
- TTFT = t(first streamed token) - t(request submitted by client), including queueing.
- TPOT = (t(last token) - t(first token)) / (output_tokens - 1), per request, then aggregated.
- End-to-end latency = TTFT + TPOT * (output_tokens - 1); report per length bucket, never pooled.
- Throughput: report input tok/s, output tok/s and req/s separately. Output tok/s is the decode capacity metric.
- Queueing delay = scheduler admission time - arrival time, exported by the engine (vLLM: time_in_queue / num_waiting), not inferred.
- P99: computed over per-request values within a stratum, with the sample count reported. P99 on <1000 samples per stratum is not trustworthy; require >=3000 requests per cell.

3. Workload control
- Fix the request-length distribution and freeze it as a replayable trace file (prompt_len, output_len, arrival offset). Do not sample a new distribution per run.
- Stratify: short-prompt/short-gen, short-prompt/long-gen, long-prompt/short-gen, long-prompt/long-gen. Report each stratum separately plus a weighted total.
- Force deterministic output length (ignore_eos + fixed max_tokens) for latency runs so decode work is not confounded by sampling variance; run a separate realistic-EOS run for capacity numbers.
- Open-loop arrivals (Poisson at target QPS) for latency, closed-loop fixed concurrency for saturation throughput. Closed-loop-only testing hides queueing and will understate P99.

4. Falsifiable hypothesis and controlled experiment
- H1: at fixed QPS, moving prefill to a separate engine pool cuts P99 TTFT by >=30% without raising P99 TPOT by more than 10%.
- Design: A/B with only the one variable changed; both arms replay the identical trace, same duration, same warmup, interleaved (ABABAB) to absorb thermal and neighbor drift. >=5 repetitions per arm.
- Warmup: discard the first 60-120 s and the first N requests until output tok/s and P50 TPOT are stationary (rolling-window slope test); report the discarded window explicitly.
- Decision rule: accept only if the effect exceeds the pre-registered threshold AND the 95% bootstrap CI of the paired per-run difference excludes zero. Otherwise the hypothesis is rejected and the change does not ship.

5. Prefill vs decode separation (mandatory in any mixed workload)
- Prefill cost scales ~O(prompt_len) compute-bound; decode is memory-bandwidth and KV-capacity bound. Pooling them produces a meaningless average.
- Attribute TTFT regressions to queueing vs prefill compute by exporting: num_waiting, num_running, scheduler step time, prefill batched tokens, preemption/recompute counters, KV cache usage %.
- Capture GPU-side evidence: nvidia-smi dmon or DCGM (SM occupancy, memory BW util, power, clocks) and per-request traces (request_id, arrival, admit, first_token, last_token, prompt_len, output_len).

6. Expected confounders
- KV-cache preemption and recomputation silently inflating TPOT tails.
- Prefix caching hits differing between arms because the trace order changed.
- Continuous batching means a request's TPOT depends on its batch neighbors; per-request TPOT is not independent, so use paired-run statistics, not per-request t-tests.
- Client-side coordinated omission if using closed-loop clients; use open-loop with fixed schedule to avoid it.
- Thermal throttling, other tenants on the node, NUMA/CPU pinning of the API server, network RTT between client and server.
- Tokenizer/detokenizer CPU cost showing up as TTFT on small models.

7. Evidence required before any claim
- Raw per-request trace files for every run, engine version/commit, exact launch flags, trace file hash, and the load generator config.
- Per-stratum tables: N, P50/P90/P99 TTFT, P50/P99 TPOT, output tok/s, queue delay, preemption count.
- GPU telemetry time series aligned to the run window.

8. Rollback criteria (pre-registered, checked in canary)
- Roll back if P99 end-to-end latency in any stratum regresses >10%, or output tok/s drops >5%, or preemption/recompute rate rises above baseline, or error/timeout rate exceeds 0.1%.
- Canary on <=5% of traffic for >=30 min covering a peak window before fleet rollout; automated rollback wired to the above SLO gates, not to a human eyeball.

9. What this plan cannot conclude
- It measures serving-system behavior only. It says nothing about model quality, and results do not transfer across model size, quantization, sequence-length regime, or GPU SKU without re-running.

- Fix the request-length distribution and freeze it as a replayable trace file (prompt_len, output_len, arrival offset). Do not sample a new distribution per run.
- Stratify: short-prompt/short-gen, short-prompt/long-gen, long-prompt/short-gen, long-prompt/long-gen. Report each stratum separately plus a weighted total.
- Force deterministic output length (ignore_eos + fixed max_tokens) for latency runs so decode work is not confounded by sampling variance; run a separate realistic-EOS run for capacity numbers.
- Open-loop arrivals (Poisson at target QPS) for latency, closed-loop fixed concurrency for saturation throughput. Closed-loop-only testing hides queueing and will understate P99.

4. Falsifiable hypothesis and controlled experiment
- H1: short requests are starved by continuous batching under long-gen load; a priority class for <256-token requests reduces their P99 by >=40% with <=5% aggregate throughput loss.
- Design: A/B with only the one variable changed; both arms replay the identical trace, same duration, same warmup, interleaved (ABABAB) to absorb thermal and neighbor drift. >=5 repetitions per arm.
- Warmup: discard the first 60-120 s and the first N requests until output tok/s and P50 TPOT are stationary (rolling-window slope test); report the discarded window explicitly.
- Decision rule: accept only if the effect exceeds the pre-registered threshold AND the 95% bootstrap CI of the paired per-run difference excludes zero. Otherwise the hypothesis is rejected and the change does not ship.

5. Prefill vs decode separation (mandatory in any mixed workload)
- Prefill cost scales ~O(prompt_len) compute-bound; decode is memory-bandwidth and KV-capacity bound. Pooling them produces a meaningless average.
- Attribute TTFT regressions to queueing vs prefill compute by exporting: num_waiting, num_running, scheduler step time, prefill batched tokens, preemption/recompute counters, KV cache usage %.
- Capture GPU-side evidence: nvidia-smi dmon or DCGM (SM occupancy, memory BW util, power, clocks) and per-request traces (request_id, arrival, admit, first_token, last_token, prompt_len, output_len).

6. Expected confounders
- KV-cache preemption and recomputation silently inflating TPOT tails.
- Prefix caching hits differing between arms because the trace order changed.
- Continuous batching means a request's TPOT depends on its batch neighbors; per-request TPOT is not independent, so use paired-run statistics, not per-request t-tests.
- Client-side coordinated omission if using closed-loop clients; use open-loop with fixed schedule to avoid it.
- Thermal throttling, other tenants on the node, NUMA/CPU pinning of the API server, network RTT between client and server.
- Tokenizer/detokenizer CPU cost showing up as TTFT on small models.

7. Evidence required before any claim
- Raw per-request trace files for every run, engine version/commit, exact launch flags, trace file hash, and the load generator config.
- Per-stratum tables: N, P50/P90/P99 TTFT, P50/P99 TPOT, output tok/s, queue delay, preemption count.
- GPU telemetry time series aligned to the run window.

8. Rollback criteria (pre-registered, checked in canary)
- Roll back if P99 end-to-end latency in any stratum regresses >10%, or output tok/s drops >5%, or preemption/recompute rate rises above baseline, or error/timeout rate exceeds 0.1%.
- Canary on <=5% of traffic for >=30 min covering a peak window before fleet rollout; automated rollback wired to the above SLO gates, not to a human eyeball.

9. What this plan cannot conclude
- It measures serving-system behavior only. It says nothing about model quality, and results do not transfer across model size, quantization, sequence-length regime, or GPU SKU without re-running.
risks: source_assistant is a grading rubric, not an answer; training on it teaches meta-commentary instead of the engineering content
no metric definitions, so TTFT/TPOT/P99 remain ambiguous and results are not comparable across runs
no rollback thresholds or canary gate, so a benchmark-driven config change could be shipped unsafely
closed-loop-only load generation would hide queueing and understate P99 (coordinated omission)
